intro: The fifty-first screen read 99 pictures, the set's 21 and 78 probes, with thirteen readers and four scorers: 1,072 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **63 of the 64 templates pass the legibility gate**, where all 64 did in v0.53. The one that fails is `square_wheel`, 0.896 in its eight pictures, and all eight are v0.53's pictures to the pixel, which v0.53's readers scored 0.938: the tier-4 playground's bicycle went from a half mark and a zero to two zeros, and one wheelbarrow from full marks to a half. Of the 30 items under full marks, twenty-six are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out, three are those square wheels', and one is a half mark on the stopped hose. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. Ninety-five of the 99 pictures are v0.53's to the pixel, and their 1,039 items are a second reading: 1,003 have the score they had, thirty-three of the 36 others are the clouds or a tree, and the other three, each down by a half mark, are the gate's failure and the hose. The set's score is 0.974, for 0.984. On the strict count 54 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.53's 56. The man in the red shirt is a man in both pictures where he sits reading and a boy in the one where he walks reading; the four grown figures are called young first in 4 of their 81 pictures, for 5 of 81.
design:
## Design tests

v0.54 changes two figures of the cast in their reading poses and no placement rule, so its whole-scene test is the bench (`vision/design_tests_v054.md`): six pictures of the man in the red shirt reading, each built with the new pose and with v0.53's, read by twelve fresh readers with the screen's own prompt. I looked at each figure with the new pose, cut out of its picture, before any reader had one, and found nothing to mend.
- **Who he is:** a man in 11 readings of 12 with his head up.
- **That he reads:** in all twelve.
- **That a walker with a book does not see the box:** in all six readings of the three pictures that hold one: "In the centre, a man in a red T-shirt and blue jeans walks fast (there are motion lines behind him) while reading an open book held in front of his face."
- **Anything new and odd about the head:** no line in any unsure section.

No picture was built again after a reading.
screen:
Across all 99 pictures 1,072 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.53: 1,084 of 1,102, none). Of the 30 under full marks:
- twenty-six are setting items that five readers left out, eighteen the clouds and eight a tree, all zeros (v0.53 had sixteen, from four readers). One reader left the clouds out of all eight of its pictures;
- two are the square-wheeled bicycle's in the tier-4 playground, both zeros: "- Red bicycle, right-front: lying on its side." and, among the unsure things, "- The bicycle could have fallen over or been laid down; nobody is near it. Perhaps it belongs to the boy at the tree.";
- one is a wheelbarrow's wheel, a half mark, named only among the unsure things: "- The wheelbarrow's wheel looks like a square frame rather than a round wheel.";
- one is the stopped hose of the tier-4 garden, a half mark: "- The dog's paw is on the hose near a joint. It could be blocking the water (which would explain the woman frowning at the nozzle) or just standing near it."

The set's headline is all items 0.974 (0.984 in v0.53). Of its 286 items eight are under full marks: the clouds in five pictures (things 0.954), the bicycle's two (contradictions 0.929) and the hose's half mark (inferences 0.984). Actions read 1.00.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.55 is `vision/flaws_v054.md`.

**The square wheel.** Eight pictures, four of the wheelbarrow and four of the bicycle, all eight v0.53's to the pixel. Three barrows and three bicycles read in full. The tier-4 playground's bicycle was not named as odd, for the second screen running and by another reader. Over the two screens and the bench that picture's bicycle was read five times: its wheels are square in the description twice, among the unsure things once, and not named twice. It is no smaller than the other bicycles, and it stands on grass as the tier-3 playground's does; what is its own is the picture, eight events with the bicycle in the front corner. The bench had already said that larger wheels are not the mend. It is first on the next list.

**A second reading of the pictures that came back.** Ninety-five of the 99 pictures are v0.53's to the pixel, nineteen of the set and 76 probes, and they hold 1,039 items. Item for item against v0.53's screen, 1,003 have the same score, twelve are higher and 24 lower. Thirty-three of the 36 are the clouds or a tree. The other three went down by a half mark each: a wheelbarrow's wheel, the tier-4 playground's bicycle and the stopped hose of the tier-4 garden. Nothing was drawn for any of them. In v0.53 the three items that moved in unchanged pictures all went up, and the gate was full; here they went down, and it is not. One reader's sentence is the size of what a screen can show, and this template sits at the gate's edge.

**The cast in the descriptions.** By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the four grown figures of v0.49's count are called by a young name first in 4 of their 81 pictures, for 5 of 81 in v0.53: the woman in purple in 2 of 25, the woman in the yellow dress in 1 of 21, the man in the red shirt in 1 of 19 (3 of 19) and the man in green in none of 16. The man sitting with a book is a man in both his pictures, his moustache named in both, where v0.53's readers of the same two pictures wrote a boy; walking with a book he is a boy still. The four are three readers' of thirteen. The moustache of the man in the red shirt is in his line in 5 of his 19 pictures (1 of 19 in v0.53), and the beard of the man in green in 12 of his 16 (9 of 16).

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers listed 82 full marks as judgement calls, for 79 in v0.53. In 42 the target stands beside another reading (32 in v0.53), and in 40 a near word or a target partly said was credited (47), twenty-three of them a word for a person. With the 42 halved, ten templates are under 0.9, and 54 of the 64 pass (56 in v0.53): the planter (0.80, on five items), the kite in the tree and the heavy seesaw (0.833 each), the dog at the door (0.85), the stopped hose, the rake and the square wheel (0.875 each), and the begging dog, the fork sweeper and the upward water (0.889 each). With all 82 halved, 44 pass (44). The four scorers listed 16, 27, 10 and 29 calls, so the strict counts compare only roughly.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 40 oddities in the 99 pictures, 0.4 a picture for v0.53's 0.3, and 8 of them in the set for 7. The readers' remarks were 2.71 per picture (2.62). What the oddities are about: figures over the pond's near edge, in six pictures, each placed on the bank by its reader; a pram drawn over a bench's back or headed for a rock, in two; a lamp post alone in the grass, in two; and a goat in a park, in two.
redrawn: No template's drawing was changed; one pose of two figures was. `read_bench`, `about_to_trip`, `bird_steals` and `sitting_on_air`, the templates that can draw a grown man reading, read 1.00 as they did. `square_wheel`, 0.938 in v0.53, reads 0.896 in the same eight pictures and is under the gate: v0.53's pass and v0.54's failure are neither of them the drawing's, which is the same. `blocked_hose` reads 0.975 in five pictures, with a half mark and four full marks beside another reading. `dog_begs`, `kite_in_tree`, `seesaw_heavy`, `dog_wants_walk`, `plant_flowers`, `rake`, `sweep_fork` and `water_upward` read 1.00 and fall under 0.9 on the strict count. It is one screen, of 3 to 24 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.17.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (33 in three, 8 in four, 16 in five, 2 in six, and one each in seven, eight, ten, thirteen and sixteen). 63 of 64 pass, where 64 did in v0.53, 63 in v0.52 and 64 in v0.51. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. Two templates are under 1.00: `square_wheel` (0.896 on twenty-four items in eight pictures, no misread), which fails, and `blocked_hose` (0.975 on twenty items in five pictures); the other 62 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v054/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 42 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 54 of the 64 pass. The square wheel's failure is on eight pictures that are v0.53's to the pixel and that v0.53's readers scored 0.938: a bicycle read as a bicycle and no more, and a barrow's wheel named only at the end. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: None of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where six had in v0.53: six moved by 0.001, in templates that draw a reader. One of the six sat on a rounding edge of the priors, which keep two places: `about_to_trip`'s inference, 0.145 to 0.146, a prior of 0.14 or of 0.15. It was left at 0.14 so that the planner draws v0.53's plans, and it did: all sixteen cells and the five isomorphs have v0.53's templates on v0.53's seeds. The calibration was measured once, with the cast as it is released (`tools/cycle/calib_cmp.py`).
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 49 with the new cast. The twelve cells of tiers 1 to 3 placed on their showcase seeds, the tier-4 park on the v0.43 seed, the tier-4 street on v0.49's, on its twenty-second step, and the tier-4 playground on v0.53's base, on its seventh step, each with v0.53's templates and v0.53's people; the tier-4 garden is v0.46's set forced on v0.46's seed, as in v0.53 (`tools/cycle/forced_cell.py`). Nineteen of the 21 pictures, the five isomorphs among them, are v0.53's to the pixel. The tier-4 street differs in one figure's head, and the tier-3 garden, which holds both men reading, placed in another layout. The probe pass built 61 and left one template short, the begging dog; two small forced groups filled it, the pass stratified by angle added 12, and three more were forced for the wheelbarrow (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 78 probes with v0.53's names, 47 gardens, 23 parks, 6 playgrounds and 2 streets, 76 of them v0.53's to the pixel. **I looked at the four pictures that changed, or the part of each that changed, beside v0.53's before any reader had them, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 99 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 355 of 355. Its soft palette warning is raised by 314 records, as in v0.53, with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
